entries.content_plain: Introduction The psalmist prays against his enemies, Psa 140:1-6 ; returns thanks for help, Psa 140:7 ; describes his enemies, and prays farther against them, Psa 140:8-11 . His confidence in God, Psa 140:12 , Psa 140:13 . The Hebrew, and all the Versions, attribute this Psalm to David; and it is supposed to contain his complaint when persecuted by Saul. The Syriac determines it to the time when Saul endeavored to transfix David with his spear. Verse 1 From the evil man - Saul, who was full of envy, jealousy, and cruelty against David, to whom both himself and his kingdom were under the highest obligations, endeavored by every means to destroy him.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 10</hi> <div eID="gen23373" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23374" type="x-p"/> Let burning coals - The Chaldee considers this as spoken against Ahithophel, who was head of a conspiracy against David; and translates this verse thus: "Let coals from heaven fall upon them, precipitate them into the fire of hell, and into miry pits, from which they shall not have a resurrection to eternal life." This is a proof that the Jews did believe in a resurrection of the body, and an eternal life for that body, in the case of the righteous.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 11</hi> <div eID="gen23374" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23375" type="x-p"/> Let not an evil speaker be established - איש לשון ish lashon, "a man of tongue." There is much force in the rendering of this clause in the Chaldee גבר דמשתעי לישן תליתי gebar demishtai lishan telithai, "The man of detraction, or inflammation, with the three-forked tongue." He whose tongue is set on fire from hell; the tale-bearer, slanderer, and dealer in scandal: with the three-forked tongue; wounding three at once: his neiphbour whom he slanders; the person who receives the slander; and himself who deals in it. What a just description of a character which God, angels, and good men must detest! Let not such a one be established in the land; let him be unmasked; let no person trust him; and let all join together to hoot him out of society. "He shall be hunted by the angel of death, and thrust into hell." - Chaldee.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 13</hi> <div eID="gen23376" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23377" type="x-p"/> The righteous shall give thanks - For thou wilt support and deliver him. <div eID="gen23377" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23378" type="x-p"/> The upright shall dwell in thy presence - Shall be admitted to the most intimate intercourse with God. <div eID="gen23378" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23379" type="x-p"/> The persecuted have ever been dear to God Almighty; and the martyrs were, in an especial manner, his delight; and in proportion as he loved those, so must he hate and detest these.  <chapter eID="Ps.140"/> <div eID="gen23379" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: Verse 13 The righteous shall give thanks - For thou wilt support and deliver him. The upright shall dwell in thy presence - Shall be admitted to the most intimate intercourse with God. The persecuted have ever been dear to God Almighty; and the martyrs were, in an especial manner, his delight; and in proportion as he loved those, so must he hate and detest these.
